newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia needs $400 bln over 20 yrs in foreign cash.
newsitem.headline: Russia needs $400 bln over 20 yrs in foreign cash.

text.p: Russia will be able to finance only about 75 percent of the cost of restructuring its economy over the next 20 years from domestic sources and will need to attract around $300-400 billion in foreign investment, minister without portfolio was quoted Yevgeny Yasin as saying on Monday.

But Itar-Tass news agency quoted Yasin as warning that despite recent positive macroeconomic developments, such as a reining in of inflation, Russia might not see a significant increase in the flow of foreign funds for several years yet.
"The foreign investor is not willing to come to Russia yet since favourable conditions for the investment of foreign capital have not been created," Yasin was quoted as saying.

Despite what both government statisticians and some independent analysts hail as a stabilisation in production and gross domestic product this year, the majority of former Soviet enterprises are hungry for investment.
Russian banks are reluctant to provide the long-term credits needed to boost output at the companies, and many are turning to banks abroad to provide loans.
